text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports right index finger pain after a skiing injury.
- history of present illness: while skiing, the patient's finger was caught in a ski strap and bent backward when going over a mogul; the injury occurred about four days before the visit. Pain persists despite ice and ibuprofen and worsens with movement.
- physical examination: tenderness over the distal phalanx and the distal interphalangeal joint; no tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal or metacarpophalangeal joints; pain on flexion; full ability to bend, extend, and touch the thumb to the finger. X-ray shows no fracture or abnormality.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right index finger pain, worse with movement.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: ibuprofen (Motrin) 600 mg every six hours for about one week.
- follow-up instructions: aluminum foam splint applied; return or call if the finger does not improve after about one week.
